match.reason: Neither bank point teaches apoptosis: mitosis covers cell division that makes identical cells, and the adaptive immune response covers antigen-targeted immunity, so no bank point teaches controlled programmed cell death.

draft.title: Apoptosis
card: Apoptosis is programmed cell death. The cell follows its own set of internal instructions and breaks itself down in a controlled way.
The cell shrinks and its contents are packaged into small pieces. Neighbouring cells or immune cells then take up these pieces, so nothing harmful spills into the tissue.

Apoptosis removes cells that are damaged, such as cells with DNA damage that cannot be repaired. It also removes cells that are no longer needed, such as the tissue between developing fingers in an embryo.
Apoptosis is different from necrosis, where a cell dies from injury and bursts open. This can release its contents and cause inflammation in the tissue around it.
draft.remember: Apoptosis is a cell's planned, tidy self-destruction, which removes cells the body does not need.

opts: A cell breaks itself down in a controlled way
A cell bursts open after a physical injury
A cell stops dividing and stays alive for good
A cell is destroyed by a toxin from outside
a.why: Apoptosis follows the cell's own internal instructions and ends with the cell packaged into pieces. Bursting open after injury describes necrosis, which is not controlled and can harm nearby cells.
a.clue: Think about who or what is in control of the cell's death.

b.q: In a human embryo, the cells between the developing fingers die and the fingers separate. Why is this best described as apoptosis?
opts: The cells die on a program because they are not needed
The cells die from injury and burst open
The cells die because their DNA has been damaged
The cells stop dividing, so the tissue shrinks away
b.why: The webbing cells are healthy but no longer needed, and they die by a controlled program. DNA damage is one trigger for apoptosis, but it is not the reason here, and the tissue is not injured.
b.clue: The cells are healthy, so look for another reason for removing them.

a.best: A cell breaks itself down in a controlled way

b.best: The cells die on a program because they are not needed
